symbol_descriptions: Differential elastic-scattering cross section with respect to squared momentum transfer, dσ/dq², in natural units
Magnitude of the momentum transfer in GeV
Dimensionless interaction coupling at each mediator-particle vertex
Composite-structure resolution scale in GeV setting the elastic form-factor turnover
Mediator mass scale in GeV controlling screening of the t-channel propagator at low transfer
derivation_notes: The dipole-like elastic suppression has been replaced by a Gaussian elastic form factor, corresponding to a different admissible smooth spatial distribution of the composite scatterer. This keeps the same propagator physics and variables but changes the resolved-structure curvature once q**2 reaches order Lambda_ff**2.
change_summary: Changed the assumption that composite structure always enters through the fixed dipole-like factor (1 + q**2/Lambda_ff**2)**(-2). Using a Gaussian elastic profile gives the same low-q**2 normalization but a different turnover and tail curvature in dsigma_dq2 versus q**2.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: The external particles' resolved internal structure is represented by the fixed factor (1 + q**2/Lambda_ff**2)**(-2) in the amplitude-squared, rather than by another physically admissible monotone elastic profile.
assumption_audit.mechanism: A different but still elastic and nonresonant spatial charge/current distribution of the composite scatterer changes the transfer-space form factor shape, modifying the q**2-dependent curvature of the differential cross section once the probe resolves internal extent.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: Both parent and child reduce to the same unsuppressed low-transfer normalization as q -> 0, where the elastic form factor tends to unity.

response_change.parent_relation: At fixed g, m_med, and Lambda_ff, dsigma_dq2 falls as a single monotone product of a screened propagator factor and one fixed dipole-like form-factor shape, so the log-slope versus q**2 changes in only one prescribed way.
response_change.child_relation: Keep the same variables but replace the current fixed form-factor profile with another admissible monotone elastic profile, changing how the suppression bends with q**2 once the transfer approaches the composite-resolution scale.
response_change.observable_effect: For q**2 comparable to Lambda_ff**2, the cross section develops a different intermediate-to-high-q**2 curvature than the parent; after matching the low-q**2 normalization and one slope scale, a single parent parameter set cannot simultaneously reproduce the altered tail steepening pattern across the same q range.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Observable when q**2 is scanned through the resolved-structure regime q**2 ~ Lambda_ff**2 to several times Lambda_ff**2, while remaining in the sampled nonzero-transfer region and with fixed g and m_med.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training, the mechanism already changes the bend of dsigma_dq2 as q**2 moves from well below to around Lambda_ff**2; in holdout at somewhat larger q**2 the same modified profile produces a systematically different tail curvature rather than a mere rescaling.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the limit where the alternative elastic profile is specialized back to the current dipole-like form-factor assumption.
evolution_contract.domain_mechanism: elastic form-factor profile change from dipole-like to Gaussian suppression
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: A different but still elastic and nonresonant spatial charge/current distribution of the composite scatterer changes the transfer-space form factor shape, modifying the q**2-dependent curvature of the differential cross section once the probe resolves internal extent.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This is harder than a coefficient-only correction because the resolved-structure suppression now depends non-polynomially on q**2/Lambda_ff**2 through a different profile, altering the turnover shape and asymptotic bend rather than merely shifting a scale or multiplying the whole response.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: The composite elastic response is locked to a dipole-like form-factor shape with denominator (1 + q**2/Lambda_ff**2)**2.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: The composite elastic response follows a different admissible monotone profile, here Gaussian in q**2/Lambda_ff**2, while keeping the same propagator structure and variables.
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: At low transfer q**2 << Lambda_ff**2, both forms approach the same leading normalization because the elastic factor tends to 1.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: The parent gives one fixed dipole-like bend in log(dsigma_dq2) versus q**2, while the child shows a different curvature once q**2 reaches order Lambda_ff**2; this changed target mapping is directly visible in dsigma_dq2(q) at fixed g and m_med, not merely in an auxiliary trajectory.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set cannot reproduce this over the resolved-structure regime because refitting Lambda_ff mainly relocates the turnover scale inside the dipole law, whereas the child changes the turnover shape and tail steepening itself. Matching near q**2 << Lambda_ff**2 and around one intermediate point still leaves systematic residual curvature differences for q**2 ~ Lambda_ff**2 to several times Lambda_ff**2.

evolution_plan.activation_condition: Observable when q**2 is scanned through the resolved-structure regime q**2 ~ Lambda_ff**2 to several times Lambda_ff**2, while remaining in the sampled nonzero-transfer region and with fixed g and m_med.
evolution_plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, the mechanism already changes the bend of dsigma_dq2 as q**2 moves from well below to around Lambda_ff**2; in holdout at somewhat larger q**2 the same modified profile produces a systematically different tail curvature rather than a mere rescaling.
evolution_plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the limit where the alternative elastic profile is specialized back to the current dipole-like form-factor assumption.
evolution_plan.gap_statement: The model assumes one specific composite elastic form-factor shape, so all structure-induced suppression is forced into a single dipole-like q**2 dependence.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: The external particles' resolved internal structure is represented by the fixed factor (1 + q**2/Lambda_ff**2)**(-2) in the amplitude-squared, rather than by another physically admissible monotone elastic profile.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: A different but still elastic and nonresonant spatial charge/current distribution of the composite scatterer changes the transfer-space form factor shape, modifying the q**2-dependent curvature of the differential cross section once the probe resolves internal extent.
evolution_plan.rationale: Parent response relationship: with g, m_med, and Lambda_ff fixed, dsigma_dq2 decreases monotonically with q through the propagator and one prescribed form-factor profile. The scientific gap is not a missing channel but an idealized assumption that the composite profile is uniquely dipole-like. A realistic next refinement is to relax that shape assumption while keeping the same static inputs. The changed target mapping is in the scored observable itself, not only in an auxiliary quantity: varying q at fixed g, m_med, and Lambda_ff produces a different curvature in dsigma_dq2 once q**2 reaches the resolution scale set by Lambda_ff. Concretely, in the admissible regime q**2 << Lambda_ff**2 both parent and child can agree closely because the form factor tends to unity, but for q**2 ~ Lambda_ff**2 and above the child shows a different rate of tail suppression. A single refitted parent parameter set cannot generally absorb this across those conditions because changing Lambda_ff mostly shifts the turnover location, whereas the refinement changes the shape of the turnover and high-q**2 bend itself. This is scientifically observable only when the sampled q range reaches the resolved-structure regime; if all data satisfy q**2 << Lambda_ff**2, the distinction becomes weak and the refinement would be hard to identify.

selected_embedding_pattern.description: Make the coefficient of an existing process depend on a declared quantity.

scenario_text: Two ultrarelativistic particles scatter through exchange of a light pointlike mediator, and the measured response is the differential cross section with respect to momentum transfer. The benchmark varies the transfer scale and interaction coupling while holding the incoming energy well above all particle masses. The exchange propagator produces a steep algebraic suppression at larger transfer. Composite structure, additional channels, and detector acceptance are treated as absent background effects.
